Your strawberry frosting containing FD&C Red No. 3 must stop being manufactured with that color additive by January 15, 2027. On that date, the removal of 21 CFR 74.303 (the listing authorizing FD&C Red No. 3 in food) takes effect, and all existing certificates for batches of FD&C Red No. 3 cease to be effective for use in food (90 FR 4628; 91 FR 50475). The administrative stay that was in place from February 18, 2025, was lifted on August 5, 2026, and the January 15, 2027 effective date was confirmed (91 FR 50475).

Regarding product already on shelves: The January 2025 order explicitly addresses this. Per 90 FR 4628: 'When FD&C Red No. 3 has been used in food or ingested drugs while its certificate is still effective, such food or ingested drugs will not be regarded as adulterated by reason of the use of such color additive.' This means frosting manufactured and colored with FD&C Red No. 3 before January 15, 2027 — while the certificate was still effective — is NOT rendered adulterated after that date. However, any food colored with FD&C Red No. 3 after January 15, 2027 will be considered adulterated because the color additive will be uncertified and its use unauthorized.

Note: The January 2025 order sets no separate compliance date; the operative deadline is derived from the effective date of January 15, 2027. There is no sell-through or phase-out period stated — the distinction is solely based on when the color additive was used (i.e., incorporated into the food), not when the finished product is sold.

response.answer:
Under the updated 'healthy' nutrient content claim rule (89 FR 106064, codified at 21 CFR 101.65(d)), a food that does not qualify for one of the automatic exemptions (e.g., single-ingredient foods from encouraged food groups, or water/tea/coffee) must meet two main criteria to bear the 'healthy' claim:

1. **Food Group Equivalent (FGE) requirement**: The food must contain a specified amount of at least one food group equivalent from the food groups encouraged by the Dietary Guidelines (vegetables, fruits, whole grains, fat-free or low-fat dairy, lean meat/seafood/eggs/beans/peas/lentils/nuts/seeds). The specific FGE amounts vary by product category (individual food, mixed product, main dish, or meal) as set forth in 21 CFR 101.65(d)(3)(ii)–(v) and the associated tables. (21 CFR 101.65(d)(2)–(3); 89 FR 106064)

2. **Nutrient-to-Limit (NTL) requirement**: The food must not exceed specified limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium, expressed as a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients. These limits also vary by product category. (21 CFR 101.65(d)(3)(ii)–(v); 89 FR 106064; see also 90 FR 10592 at passage describing the rule as requiring 'FGEs and specific limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients')

As summarized in the background section of 90 FR 10592 (Doc. 2025-03118): the rule 'requires that, to bear a claim subject to the rule, individual food products, mixed products, main dishes, and meals must meet FGEs and specific limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients.'

answer_rows.required_change: Food must (1) contain a qualifying food group equivalent (FGE) amount and (2) meet nutrient-to-limit (NTL) caps for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium, unless it qualifies for an automatic exemption (single-ingredient encouraged foods or water/tea/coffee).

response.answer: Your colleague is incorrect. The administrative stay did NOT change the deadline. response.answer:
No, that was not a fair reading in mid-2025, and it is definitively incorrect now.

**What was true in mid-2025:** The January 2025 order revoking FD&C Red No. 3 (90 FR 4628, published 2025-01-16, Doc. 2025-00830) was subject to an automatic administrative stay under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) as of February 18, 2025, triggered by the filing of objections. During that stay, the effective dates of January 15, 2027 (food uses, removal of 21 CFR 74.303) and January 18, 2028 (ingested drugs, removal of 21 CFR 74.1303) were suspended pending FDA's resolution of the objections. However, the order itself was a final binding order — not a proposal — and the stay was a procedural pause, not a substantive reversal. The stay did not vacate the order or render it non-final; it merely suspended its operation temporarily. Saying the removal was 'not final and might never take effect' overstated the legal situation. The order was final on publication; the stay only delayed its operative force while objections were adjudicated.

**What is the position now:** FDA published a document on August 5, 2026 (91 FR 50475, Doc. 2026-15920) that overruled all objections, denied requests for a public hearing, and lifted the administrative stay. Critically, FDA confirmed the original effective dates without modification: January 15, 2027 for food (§ 74.303) and January 18, 2028 for ingested drugs (§ 74.1303). The document states: 'we are ending the administrative stay of the January 2025 order, and under the January 2025 order we are repealing the listing for FD&C Red No. 3 in § 74.303 as a color additive in food and § 74.1303 as a color additive in ingested drugs effective January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028, respectively' (91 FR 50475). This constitutes 'final action on the objections' under section 701(e)(2) of the FD&C Act.

The revocation is therefore fully confirmed and binding. No compliance date was separately stated; the operative deadlines are derived from the effective dates. After January 15, 2027, any food containing FD&C Red No. 3 will be adulterated (90 FR 4628 at section VI). After January 18, 2028, the same applies to ingested drugs.

response.answer:
The order published at 90 FR 4628 (Doc. 2025-00830, published January 16, 2025) changes three CFR provisions within 21 CFR Part 74, and they do NOT all change on the same day. The amendatory instructions are:

1. **Amendatory Instruction 2 – Remove 21 CFR 74.303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for food use). This removes the entire listing that authorizes FD&C Red No. 3 as a color additive in food (including dietary supplements). Effective date: **January 15, 2027** (90 FR 4628; confirmed by 91 FR 50475).

2. **Amendatory Instruction 3 – Revise 21 CFR 74.1303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for ingested drugs). Because § 74.1303 currently cross-references the identity and specifications in § 74.303(a)(1) and (b), the order revises § 74.1303 to incorporate that identity and specification language directly, so the ingested-drug listing remains self-contained after § 74.303 is removed. Effective date: **January 15, 2027** (90 FR 4628; passage 2025-00830#0021).

3. **Amendatory Instruction 4 – Remove 21 CFR 74.1303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for ingested drugs). This removes the entire listing that authorizes FD&C Red No. 3 as a color additive in ingested drugs. Effective date: **January 18, 2028** (90 FR 4628; confirmed by 91 FR 50475).

Thus, the provisions do NOT all change on the same day. Instructions 2 and 3 take effect January 15, 2027, while instruction 4 takes effect January 18, 2028. The order sets no separate compliance dates; the deadlines are derived from the effective dates—once a listing is removed, any food or drug containing FD&C Red No. 3 is adulterated (passage 2025-00830#0021). An administrative stay under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) was in effect from February 18, 2025, through August 5, 2026, but FDA lifted the stay and confirmed both effective dates unchanged (91 FR 50475, Doc. 2026-15920).

response.answer: Under 21 CFR 101.65(a)(2), a 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim must be made in accordance with the general requirements for nutrient content claims in § 101.13, with one specific carve-out: § 101.13(h) is excepted when the nutrient content claim is made in accordance with paragraph (d) of § 101.65. Section 101.13(h) is the disclosure requirement that would otherwise mandate a statement such as 'See nutrition information for ___ content' when a food exceeds specified levels of fat, saturated fat, cholesterol, or sodium. This disclosure requirement does not apply to foods bearing the 'healthy' claim under § 101.65(d). All other provisions of § 101.13 — including requirements on claim type size (§ 101.13(f)), the general prohibition on nutrient content claims not made in accordance with subpart D (§ 101.13(b)), and other general principles — remain applicable to 'healthy' claims.

response.answer: Yes, your shelf-stable lentil soup labeled 'healthy' is affected by the updated definition of the term 'healthy' under the final rule published at 89 FR 106064 (Doc. 2024-29957, published 2024-12-27). This rule revises 21 CFR 101.65(d) to establish new food-group-equivalent (FGE) and nutrient-to-limit (NTL) criteria for foods bearing the 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim. Under the new framework, your lentil soup would need to qualify under one of the pathways in § 101.65(d)(3): either as a food comprised solely of qualifying ingredients with no other added ingredients except water (paragraph (d)(3)(i)), or by meeting the applicable FGE and NTL requirements for individual foods (paragraph (d)(3)(ii)), or as a mixed product (paragraph (d)(3)(iii)), depending on its composition. Lentils are listed among the qualifying foods in paragraph (d)(3)(i)(E), but if your soup contains other added ingredients beyond those listed (e.g., salt, oil, seasonings), it would not qualify under the automatic pathway and would instead need to meet the FGE and NTL thresholds (including limits on added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium) applicable to its product category. The effective date of the rule is April 28, 2025 (as delayed by 90 FR 10592, Doc. 2025-03118). The compliance date is February 25, 2028, as stated in the final rule (89 FR 106064). Until that compliance date, you may continue to use the 'healthy' claim under the prior criteria, but by February 25, 2028, your product must meet the updated requirements of 21 CFR 101.65(d) or you must remove the 'healthy' claim from the label.

Your supplier is partially correct in a narrow technical sense but draws the wrong practical conclusion. The Red No. 3 order (Doc. 2025-00830, 90 FR 4628, published 2025-01-16) indeed sets no explicit 'compliance date' — it states only effective dates. However, the absence of a compliance date does NOT mean there is no hard deadline. Once the effective date arrives, the listing in 21 CFR 74.303 is removed, and any food containing FD&C Red No. 3 becomes adulterated under the FD&C Act. The operative deadline is therefore derived from the effective date: January 15, 2027 for food uses (all provisions except amendatory instruction 4), and January 18, 2028 for ingested drug uses (removal of 21 CFR 74.1303). After January 15, 2027, food products colored with Red No. 3 would be adulterated regardless of when they were manufactured or when inventory was acquired.

Important caveat: An administrative stay under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) was in effect from February 18, 2025 through August 5, 2026 (per timeline source citing Doc. 2026-15920). That stay has now ended (in_force_now: false), and the stay did not change the stated dates (dates_changed: false). Therefore the January 15, 2027 effective date for food uses remains operative.

In summary: there is no stated compliance date, but there IS a hard deadline — it is derived from the effective date of January 15, 2027 for foods. After that date, the color additive listing no longer exists and products containing Red No. 3 are adulterated. Your supplier's conclusion that there is 'no hard deadline' is incorrect.

answer_rows.product: Any food product containing FD&C Red No. 3
answer_rows.trigger: Removal of 21 CFR 74.303 (food use listing for FD&C Red No. 3)
answer_rows.required_change: Reformulate to eliminate FD&C Red No. 3 from all food products; exhaust or dispose of colored inventory before the effective date

response.answer: Your compliance memo's recorded date of January 15, 2025 is incorrect. The Red No. 3 revocation order (Document No. 2025-00830) was published in the Federal Register on January 16, 2025, at 90 FR 4628. This is confirmed by both the order itself (90 FR 4628) and the subsequent order lifting the administrative stay (91 FR 50475, published August 5, 2026), which repeatedly references 'the order that published in the Federal Register of January 16, 2025 (90 FR 4628).' The date January 15, 2027 is the effective date for the food-use provisions, not the publication date.
